# ON GOETIA AND NECROMANCY

<page-num>355</page-num>
-> ON GOETIA AND NECROMANCY <-

These magicians study not only natural things, but also those things that accompany nature and, in a certain way, strip it bare—such as motions, numbers, figures, sounds, voices, harmonies, lights, the passions of the mind, and words. Thus the Psylli and the Marsi <note>Ancient tribes renowned for their power over snakes</note> used to summon serpents, while others drove them away by subduing them. Thus Orpheus calmed the storm of the Argonauts with a hymn; and Homer relates that for Ulysses, blood was restrained by words <note>original: "sanguinem verbis restrictum"</note>. In the Law of the Twelve Tables <note>The earliest code of Roman law</note>, a penalty was established for those who had "enchanted away" harvests. Thus there is no doubt that magicians, by words and passions alone, and other similar means, often produce some wonderful effect—not only upon themselves, but even upon external objects. They believe that all these things pour out an innate power into other things, drawing them toward themselves or repelling them, or affecting them in any other way, no differently than a magnet draws iron or amber draws chaff, or as a diamond and garlic bind the magnet <note>A common medieval belief that garlic or diamonds could neutralize magnetic force</note>. And so, through this gradual and linked sympathy of things, Iamblichus, Proclus, and Synesius <note>Neoplatonic philosophers who wrote on theurgy and the soul</note> confirm that, according to the opinion of magicians, not only natural and celestial gifts but even intellectual and divine ones can be received from above. Proclus confesses this in his book *On Sacrifice and Magic*, namely, that through this kind of consensus of things, magicians were also accustomed to summon deities. For some of them have fallen into such madness that they think an image, constructed from various constellations of stars at specific intervals of time and with a duly observed ratio of proportions, will receive a spirit of life and intellect by the nod of the heavens, so that it may answer those consulting it and reveal the secrets of hidden truth. From this it is clear that this natural magic sometimes inclines toward goetia <note>term: Goetia (low magic or sorcery involving the invocation of spirits)</note> and theurgy <note>term: Theurgy (high magic aimed at union with the divine)</note>, and is very often ensnared by the deceits and errors of evil demons.

## ON GOETIA AND NECROMANCY.

<image-desc>A decorative historiated initial 'C' featuring a woodcut of a seated child or putto, possibly holding a book or cloth, set within a square frame.</image-desc>The parts of ceremonial magic, however, are goetia and theurgy. Goetia is unfortunate in its commerce with impure spirits; it is composed of the nefarious rites of curiosity, illicit incantations, and deprecations, and has been exterminated and execrated by the decrees of all laws. To this class belong those whom we today call necromancers and sorcerers.

> A race hated by the gods, skilled in staining the heavens,
> Whom nature brought forth as an evil, who can pervert
> The stars of the world and the laws of fixed things.
> For now they know how to make the poles stand still, and send forth rivers,
> They drive the ether beneath the earth, and tear up mountains.

These are they, therefore, who call upon the souls of the dead, and those whom the ancients called *epodos* <note>enchanters</note>, who enchant boys and draw them into the speech of an oracle, and those who carry about "assistant demons" <note>original: "daemones paredros"</note>, such as we read something of regarding Socrates. There are also those who, as it is said, feed spirits in glass vessels, through which they falsely claim to prophesy. And all these proceed in two ways. For some study to summon and compel evil demons, adjured by the power of especially divine names; for since every creature fears and reveres the name of Him who made it, it is no wonder if practitioners of goetia—and even those who are infidels, pagans, Jews, Saracens, and any profane assembly—

<note>original: "Goëtia"</note> <term>Goetia</term> <note>A term derived from the Greek word for wailing or moaning, used to describe "low" magic or the conjuration of spirits, often contrasted with Theurgy or "high" divine magic.</note> or sect, men bind demons by invoking the divine name. Others, however, most wicked and deserving of punishment by every fire for their detestable crime, submit themselves to demons, sacrificing to and worshipping them; these have become guilty of idolatry and the most base degradation. Even if the former group <note>those who merely "bind" spirits</note> are not liable for these specific crimes, they nevertheless expose themselves to manifest dangers. For even when coerced, demons remain watchful, always seeking to deceive us as we wander. Indeed, from the assembly of these practitioners of Goetia have flowed all those books of darkness, which the legal expert <term>Ulpian</term> <note>Domitius Ulpianus, a famous 3rd-century Roman jurist known for his strict stance against magic and forbidden texts.</note> calls "writings of disapproved reading," and which he decreed should be immediately destroyed.

A certain Zabulus, devoted to illicit arts, is said to have first devised such things, followed by a certain Barnabas of Cyprus. Even today, books are circulated under forged titles, using the names of Adam, Abel, Enoch, Abraham, and Solomon; likewise Paul, Honorius, Cyprian, Albert, Thomas, Jerome, and a certain person of York. King Alfonso of Castile, Robert the Englishman, Bacon, and Abano <note>Pietro d'Abano, a 13th-century philosopher and physician often accused of magic.</note>, and many other men of lamented genius, have foolishly followed the trifles of these authors. Furthermore, they have not only made men, saints, patriarchs, and angels of God the authors of such execrable doctrines, but they even show off books supposedly delivered by the angels Raziel and Raphael to Adam and Tobias. 

However, to anyone looking more closely, the rule of their teachings, their rituals, customs, the types of words and characters used, the order of construction, and their tasteless phrasing openly betray themselves. They contain nothing but mere trifles and impostures, concocted in later times by the most ruinous masters of perdition who were ignorant of all ancient magic. These works are grafted together from certain profane observations mixed with the ceremonies of our religion, using many unknown names and seals to terrify the unrefined and simple, and to strike wonder into the senseless and those who do not know good literature. 

Yet, it is not evident from this that these arts are merely fables; for if they were not real, and if many wonderful and harmful things were not done through them, divine and human laws would not have decreed so strictly that they must be exterminated from the earth. The reason why these practitioners of Goetia use only evil demons is because good angels rarely appear; they wait for God’s command and only associate with men who are pure of heart and holy of life. Evil spirits, however, show themselves easily to those who invoke them, falsely favoring them and lying about their divinity, always ready to deceive by their cunning so that they may be venerated and adored. 

And because women are more greedy for secrets, less cautious, and prone to superstition, they are more easily deluded; therefore, the spirits present themselves more readily to them and perform great wonders. The poets sing of such things regarding Circe and Medea; Cicero, Pliny, Seneca, Augustine, and many others—both philosophers and Catholic doctors and historians—bear witness to this, as do the Holy Scriptures themselves. For in the Books of Kings, we read that the <term>Pythoness</term> <note>The Witch of Endor; "Pythoness" was a common term for a woman with a familiar spirit or one who practiced divination.</note> woman who was in Endor called forth the soul of the prophet Samuel, although many interpret this to mean it was not the soul of the prophet, but a malignant spirit who took on his image. Nevertheless, the Hebrew masters say—and even Augustine does not deny the possibility in his writings to Simplicianus—that it was the true spirit of Samuel, because before a full year had passed since his departure...

# 357.
# ON THEURGY.

The soul can be easily called forth from the body, just as the practitioners of <term>Goetia</term> <note>Low magic or sorcery, often associated with the conjuration of evil spirits.</note> teach. Indeed, even the magi and necromancers believe this can be done through certain natural forces and bonds, as we ourselves discuss in our books on *Occult Philosophy*. Therefore, the ancient fathers, who were skilled in spiritual matters, established—not without cause—that the bodies of the dead should be buried in a sacred place, accompanied by lights, sprinkled with holy water, perfumed with frankincense and incense, and purified with prayers for as long as they remain upon the earth. 

For as the masters of the Hebrews say, our entire body, the fleshly animal, and whatever in us rests upon the ill-disposed matter of the flesh, is left as food for the serpent, and for him whom they call <term>Azazel</term> <note>In this context, a demonic figure or scapegoat spirit representing the corruption of the material world.</note>, who is the lord of flesh and blood and the prince of this world. In Leviticus, he is called the prince of the deserts, to whom it was said in Genesis: *You shall eat the earth all the days of your life.* And in Isaiah: *Dust is your bread.* This refers to our body created from the dust of the earth, <term>so long as</term> <note>original: "q̃ diu"</note> it has not been sanctified and transformed into something better, so that it is no longer the serpent’s but has become God’s—namely, changed from fleshly to spiritual. This follows the word of Paul, who says: *It is sown a natural body, and it shall rise a spiritual body.* And elsewhere: *We shall all indeed rise, but we shall not all be changed,* because many are destined to remain forever as food for the serpent. 

Thus, we lay down this foul and horrid matter of the flesh and the serpent's food at death, intending to take it up again one day when it has been transformed into a better and spiritual lot, which shall occur in the resurrection of the dead. This has already happened in those who have tasted the first fruits of the resurrection; many have attained this very thing in this life by the power of the deifying spirit, such as Enoch, Elijah, and Moses, whose bodies—transformed into a spiritual nature—did not see corruption, nor were they left to the power of the serpent like other corpses. And this is that dispute between the devil and Michael over the body of Moses, which Jude mentions in his epistle. But enough has been said of <term>Goetia</term> and <term>Necromancy</term>.

## ON THEURGY.

<image-desc>Ornate woodcut drop cap 'T' featuring a small winged child or putto riding on the back of a sea creature or dolphin amidst waves.</image-desc>

Theurgy, however, is thought by many to be by no means illicit, as if it were governed by good angels and the divine spirit. Yet, very often, under the names of God and angels, it is bound up in the wicked deceptions of demons. For we win over and attract celestial powers—and through them, divine virtues—to ourselves, not only by natural forces but also by certain rites and ceremonies. The ancient magi treated these in many rules within their published volumes. 

The greatest part of all ceremonies consists in maintaining cleanliness: first of the soul, then also of the body and those things which surround the body, such as the skin, clothes, dwellings, vessels, utensils, offerings, victims, and sacrifices. The cleanliness of these things prepares one for the habit and contemplation of divine matters and is most greatly demanded in sacred rites, according to the words of Isaiah: *Wash yourselves and be clean, and take away the evil of your thoughts.* Indeed, because uncleanness frequently infects both the air and the person, it disturbs that most pure influx of celestial and divine things, and [drives away] the pure spirits of God...

CCCLVIII.

# ON THE KABBALAH.

<note>original: "DE CABALA"</note>

...drives away rituals. Truly, sometimes impure spirits and deceptive powers, in order to be venerated and adored as gods, also demand this purity; therefore, the greatest caution is needed here, concerning which we have discussed extensively in our books *On Occult Philosophy*. Truly, Porphyry <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher (c. 234–305 AD) who wrote on theurgy and the soul.</note>, disputing many things about this theurgy <term>theurgy: a form of high magic intended to invoke the presence of divine beings or gods</term>, or divine magic, finally concludes that through theurgical consecrations the soul of a man can indeed be rendered fit for the reception of spirits and angels, and for seeing the gods; but he utterly denies that a return to God can be provided by this art. Of its school, therefore, are the *Art of the Almadel*, the *Notary Art*, the *Pauline Art*, the *Art of Revelations*, and many such superstitions, which are all the more pernicious because they appear more divine to the unskilled.

## ON THE KABBALAH.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'V' featuring a detailed landscape engraving with a castle or fortified town on a hill, surrounded by trees and foliage.</image-desc>But here the words of Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, Roman naturalist and author.</note> occur to me, who says: "There is also another faction of magic, depending even now upon Moses and Latopea, who were Jews." These words remind me of the Kabbalah of the Jews, which is a firm opinion among the Hebrews was given by God himself to Moses on Mount Sinai, and thereafter through a succession of degrees, without written monuments, was handed down to posterity by living voice alone until the times of Ezra. Just as the Pythagorean dogmas were once handed down by Archippus and Lysis, who held schools in Thebes in Greece, in which the disciples, holding the precepts of the teachers by heart, used their intellect and memory instead of books; so also certain Jews, scorning letters, placed this in memory, observation, and vocal tradition. Hence it is called "Kabbalah" by the Hebrews, as if it were the reception of one from another by hearing alone. It is an art (as it is said) ancient, but the name was not known among Christians until recent times. 

<margin>Kabbalah is twofold.</margin> Indeed, they hand down a twofold knowledge of it: one concerning *Bereshit* <note>original: "Breſith" - referring to the first part of the Kabbalah dealing with the "Work of Creation" (Genesis).</note>, which they also call cosmology, namely, explaining the powers of natural and celestial created things, and expounding the secrets of the Law and the Bible by philosophical reasons. In this respect, it differs in no way from natural magic, in which we believe King Solomon excelled. For it is read in the sacred histories of the Hebrews that he used to dispute from the cedar of Lebanon even unto the hyssop; likewise of beasts, birds, reptiles, and fish, all of which can display certain magical powers of nature. Moses the Egyptian <note>Maimonides (1138–1204), the famous Jewish philosopher.</note> himself, among the later writers, followed this in his expositions upon the Pentateuch <note>The first five books of the Bible.</note>, as did many Talmudists. 

But the other part of its science they call *Merkavah* <note>original: "Mercaua" - referring to the "Work of the Chariot," the mystical study of the divine realm and the throne of God.</note>, which is concerning the more sublime contemplations of divine and angelic virtues, and of sacred names and seals; a certain kind of symbolic theology, as it were, in which letters, numbers, figures, things and names, and the tips of elements, and lines, points, and accents, are all significant of the most profound things and great secrets. This they again cut into two parts: into Arithmancy <note>Divination by numbers.</note>, namely that which is called *Notaricon* <term>Notaricon: a Kabbalistic method of deriving new words or meanings from the initials or endings of words</term>, treating of angelic virtues, names, and seals, and even the conditions of demons and souls; and into Theomancy, which searches into the mysteries of the divine majesty, emanations, sacred names, and pentacles. He who knows this, they say, is powerful with wonderful virtues, so that when he wishes, he may foreknow all future things and command all of nature...

# CCCLIX.

-> ON THE CABALA <-

<note>original: "DE CABALA"</note>

...that he might have power over spirits and angels, and perform miracles. By this <term>Cabala</term><note>The Jewish mystical tradition</note> they believe Moses performed so many signs: turning his staff into a serpent, and the waters into blood; sending frogs, flies, lice, locusts, and caterpillars <note>ink smudge</note> then with hail, sending blisters and wasting diseases upon the Egyptians; slaying every firstborn from man to beast; and while leading his people out, opening the sea, bringing forth a spring from the rock, and quails from heaven; sweetening bitter waters; promising lightning and clouds by day, and a pillar of fire by night to his people; calling down the voice of the living God to the people from the heavens; striking the arrogant with fire and the murmurers with leprosy; afflicting the undeserving with sudden slaughter and others by being swallowed in a gap in the earth; feeding the people with heavenly food; calming serpents; curing the poisoned; preserving a vast multitude from infirmity and their garments from wearing away; and rendering them victorious over their enemies. Finally, by this art of miracles, Joshua commanded the sun to stand still, Elijah called down fire from heaven upon his adversaries and restored a dead boy to life, Daniel stroked the mouths of lions, and the three boys played songs in the furnace of a glowing fire. Furthermore, the faithless Jews maintain that by this art even Christ performed such admirable things so often, and that Solomon also was highly skilled in it, and from it handed down an art against demons—both their bonds and methods of incantation—and charms against diseases, as Josephus <note>Flavius Josephus, the 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian</note> is the authority. 

But while I do not doubt that God revealed many mysteries to Moses and the other prophets which were contained "under the husk" of the words of the Law and not to be communicated to the profane masses, yet this art of Cabala which the Hebrews boast of—which I once scrutinized with much labor—I recognize as nothing but a mere rhapsody of superstition and a kind of <term>theurgic magic</term><note>Ritual magic intended to invoke spirits or gods</note>. For if (as the Jews boast) it proceeded from God for the perfection of life, the salvation of men, the worship of God, and the understanding of truth, surely that Spirit of Truth, who came to teach us all truth after the Synagogue was rejected, would not have hidden this from His Church until these final times. For the Church surely knows all things that are of God, whose blessing, baptism, and other sacraments of salvation have been revealed and perfected in every language. For the power of each and every language is equal and the same, provided the piety is equal and the same; nor is there any other name in heaven or on earth in which we must be saved, and in which we work virtue, except the one name of Jesus, in whom all things are gathered and contained. Hence the Jews, though most skilled in the divine names, can work little or nothing after Christ, just as their ancient fathers did. 

As for what we experience and see in the "revolutions" <note>The rearrangement of letters</note> of this art (as they call it), where often wondrous sentences of great mysteries are extorted from the sacred scriptures, all of this is nothing other than a kind of play of allegories. Idle men, occupied with individual letters, points, and numbers—which this language and style of writing easily allow—fashion and refashion these things according to their own judgment. Even if these things sometimes sound like great mysteries, they can nevertheless prove or evince nothing; indeed, according to the words of Gregory <note>Likely Pope Gregory the Great</note>, one may despise them with the same ease with which they are asserted. The monk Rabanus <note>Rabanus Maurus, a 9th-century scholar known for his "carmina figurata" or shape poems</note> fashioned many similar things with a similar artifice, but using Latin characters and verses, inserting various images which, read in any direction through any lines of the surface and figures, announce some sacred mystery representing the history depicted there; which even from profane literature are extort-

# 360.
## ON THE KABBALAH.

No one is unaware that such things can be done, if they have read the *centones* <note>original: "centones"; a literary work made up of excerpts from other authors. Here, it refers to Proba's 4th-century poem rearranging Virgil's lines to tell the story of Christ.</note> composed by Valeria Proba from the poems of Virgil; all of these are merely the speculations of idle men. However, as far as the performance of miracles is concerned, I think none of you are so stiff-necked as to believe that any art or science exists for such things. Therefore, this Jewish Kabbalah <term>Kabbalah: a school of Jewish mysticism; the author here views it skeptically as a manipulation of text rather than divine revelation.</term> is nothing other than a most pernicious superstition. By it, they collect, divide, and transfer words, names, and letters scattered throughout the scriptures according to their own whim. By making one thing out of another, they dismember the limbs of truth, constructing speeches, inductions, and parables from their own fictions. They wish to adapt the eloquence of God to these fictions, defaming the scriptures and claiming their own figments are contained within them. They misrepresent the law of God, and through impudently extorted calculations of words, syllables, letters, and numbers, they attempt to introduce violent and blasphemous proofs for their own faithlessness.

Furthermore, puffed up by these trifles, they boast that they find and know the ineffable mysteries of God and secrets that are beyond the scripture. Through these, they do not blush to lie with great audacity—without a reddening of the face—claiming that they can prophesy and perform virtues and miracles. But it happens to them as it did to Aesop's dog <note>A reference to the fable of the dog and its reflection.</note>, who, leaving the bread behind and gaping at its shadow, lost the food itself. Thus, this faithless and stiff-necked race of men, always occupied with the shadows of scripture and making an assault upon those vanities with their ingenious but superstitious Kabbalah, loses the bread of eternal life; feeding on empty names, they lose the word of truth.

From this Jewish leaven of Kabbalistic superstition, I believe, emerged the Ophites, Gnostics, and Valentinian heretics <note>Early Christian sects often labeled as heretical for their secret knowledge (gnosis) and complex cosmologies.</note>. They too, with their disciples, devised a certain Greek Kabbalah, perverting all the mysteries of the Christian faith and, with heretical depravity, dragging them down to Greek letters and numbers. From these they construct a body which they call "Truth," teaching that without these mysteries of letters and numbers, the truth cannot be found in the Gospel writings. They claim the Gospels are varied and sometimes contradictory, written full of parables so that "those seeing may not see, and those hearing may not hear, and those understanding may not understand," but are set forth for the blind and wandering according to the capacity of their blindness and error. They believe the sincere truth lying hidden beneath these is entrusted only to the "perfect," not through writings, but through the successive pronunciation of the living voice. They claim this is that alphabetic and arithmetic theology which Christ manifested secretly to the apostles, and which Paul says he speaks only among the perfect. For since these are the highest mysteries, they are neither written nor to be written, but are to be kept in silence among the wise, guarding them in secret within themselves. Yet, among them, no one is "wise" unless he knows how to manufacture the greatest monsters of heresy.

### ON ILLUSIONS.

But let us return to magic, a small part of which is the art of illusions <term>original: "praestigiorum"; refers to sleight of hand or deceptive appearances.</term>—that is, of deceptions which occur only according to appearance. By these, magi produce phantasms and many miracles through the tricks of traveling performers...

# ON ILLUSIONS.

They play with frauds and send dreams, which is achieved not only by sorcerous incantations <note>original: "goëticis incantamentis"</note> and imprecations, and the deceits of demons, but also by certain vapors of fumigations, lights, leaves, eye-salves, bindings, and suspensions; furthermore, it is performed through rings, images, mirrors, and similar medicines and instruments of the magical art, by natural and celestial power. Many things are also done with a ready subtlety and industry of the hands, the kind we see daily performed by actors and jugglers, whom we therefore call <term>chirosophos</term> <note>Greek: "hand-wise" or sleight-of-hand experts</note>. There exist books of illusions on this craft by <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Hermeticism</note> and certain others. We also read that a certain illusionist named <term>Pasetes</term> was accustomed to show a banquet-hall filled with guests, and when he pleased, it vanished again, leaving all the diners mocked by hunger and thirst. We read that <term>Numa Pompilius</term> <note>The second king of Rome, often associated with religious and magical rites</note> also used illusions of this kind. But even the most learned <term>Pythagoras</term> <note>The famous Greek philosopher and mathematician</note> sometimes practiced this trick: he would write whatever he liked in blood on a mirror, and when this was turned toward the orb of the full moon, he would show the things inscribed to someone standing behind him as if they were on the disk of the moon. To this also belongs whatever is commonly sung by poets, believed by historians, and asserted by some Christian theologians—and even by the Holy Scriptures—concerning the transformations of men. Thus, men appear as donkeys or horses or other animals because the eyes are fascinated <note>enchanted or deceived</note> or the medium is disturbed, and this by natural art. Sometimes these things are also done by good and evil spirits, or at the prayers of the good by God himself, as we read in the Holy Scriptures concerning the prophet <term>Elisha</term>, when he was besieged by the army of the King of Syria surrounding <term>Dothan</term>. Truly, these things cannot deceive eyes that are pure and opened by God; thus that woman, who was judged by the common people to be a beast of burden, appeared to <term>Hilarion</term> <note>St. Hilarion, a 4th-century hermit</note> not as a beast, but as what she was: a woman. Therefore, those things which happen in this way according to appearance are called illusions <note>original: "praestigia"</note>. Those things which are done by the art of those who change or transfer things—such as concerning <term>Nebuchadnezzar</term>, or harvests moved to other fields—we have spoken of these above. Truly, concerning this art of illusions, <term>Iamblichus</term> <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote on theurgy and mysteries</note> says: "Those things which the enchanted or fascinated imagine have no truth of action or essence beyond the imagination." For the end of such an art is not to simply *make*, but to offer imaginings for the sake of appearance, of which soon no trace remains. Now, therefore, from these things which have been said, it is clear that magic is nothing other than a complex of idolatry, astrology, and superstitious medicine. And now, from the magicians, a great crowd of heretics has arisen in the Church, who, just as <term>Jannes and Jambres</term> <note>The Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses</note> resisted <term>Moses</term>, so they resisted the apostolic truth. The prince of these was <term>Simon the Samaritan</term> <note>Simon Magus, often called the "Father of Heresies"</note>, who at Rome under <term>Claudius Caesar</term> was granted a statue because of this art, with this inscription: *To Simon the holy god*. His blasphemies are recounted at length by <term>Clement</term>, <term>Eusebius</term>, and <term>Irenaeus</term>. From this Simon, as if from a nursery of all heresies, through many successions came forth the monstrous <term>Ophites</term>, the filthy <term>Gnostics</term>, the impious <term>Valentinians</term>, <term>Cerdonians</term>, <term>Marcionites</term>, <term>Montanists</term>, and many other heretics, lying against God for the sake of gain and empty glory, bringing no utility...

# ON DECEPTIONS

...nor do they bestow benefits upon men, but rather they deceive them, leading them into destruction and error; and those who believe in them shall be confounded in the judgment of God. Indeed, while I was still a youth, I wrote three books on magical matters of a quite ample size, which I titled *On Occult Philosophy* <note>Latin: "De Occulta Philosophia," Agrippa's most famous work on magic, published in 1533</note>. In these books, whatever errors I committed through the curiosity of my adolescence, I now, being more cautious, wish to take back by this retraction <note>original: "palinodia," a formal recantation or "singing again" of one's views</note>. For I once wasted a great deal of time and resources on these vanities. At last, I have gained this much: that I know by what arguments others ought to be discouraged from this destruction. For whoever presumes to divine and prophesy—not in the truth nor in the power of God, but in the delusion of demons according to the operation of evil spirits—and those who practice magical vanities, exorcisms, incantations, love potions, spells of attraction <term>agogima: ancient Greek spells intended to "lead" or forcibly bring a lover to the practitioner</term>, and other demoniacal works and frauds of idolatry,
